analysis.title: The Flow Show: When AI met ABB
key_insights: YTD 2026 returns: oil +79.1%, US stocks +12.7%, global stocks +9.6%, US$ +3.7%, cash +3.1%, HY bonds -0.5%, IG -2.5%, govt bonds -3.3%, gold -7.1%, bitcoin -8.4%.

Over the past six months there were 42 global central bank hikes. The US$ and UST yields have risen for four months, and tech leadership has stalled (NDX 30k cap, SOX -20%). BofA calls this classic painful tightening that is not mortal unless job losses or a credit event occur.
The next big risk-on allocation move awaits the end of hikes and a collapse in oil in H1'27. Key levels to hold before a year-end rally: MAGS $70 (Mag7) and SMH $520 (semis).

Markets are pricing a risk-off Democratic sweep in the midterms (Polymarket odds in Table 2), but not a DEM wave of +53 Senate seats or a jump in bond yields. Voter demand for 'affordability' is negative for tech, bank and energy monopolies in '27 and positive for consumer discretionary.

China: new low bond yields, CNY up more than 20% vs the Taiwan dollar over the past year, China tech (CQQQ) -32% since June. China financials have doubled in three years. BofA is short oil in H1'27 as peace boosts supply. If lower oil does not trigger a Euro and Yen bounce, that would signal China deflation is a new global negative.

Buy tech bonds as 'diamonds in the rough': US tech bonds are -9% YTD, and relative return to the IG bond index is at 30-year lows. AI hyperscaler debt issuance surged to $182bn in '26 vs $17bn in '24. Mag7 bond yields of 6-8% are attractive (Table 1).

Hyperscaler equity issuance of $89bn in '26, with buybacks running at $14bn YTD annualized vs $105bn in '24, means the era of big stock buybacks is over. META equity issuance signals new respect for credit investors.
Weekly flows: $56.2bn to stocks, $15.4bn to bonds, $3.4bn to cash, $0.5bn out of crypto, $1.7bn out of gold. Gold saw its first outflow since Jul'26.

Regional flows: China +$25.7bn (biggest since Apr'25, 'national team' buying), Japan +$6.8bn (biggest inflow since May'13), Europe -$2.3bn (biggest outflow since Jul'26), tech +$5.3bn (5th straight week of inflows), materials -$1.2bn (biggest outflow since Jul'26).

BofA private clients ($4.6tn AUM) are 66.0% stocks, 17.5% bonds and 9.4% cash. They had the 2nd highest weekly equity inflow ever, driven by IPO proceeds. They bought municipal bond, industrials and healthcare ETFs and sold staples, EM debt and consumer discretionary ETFs.
Bull & Bear Indicator fell to 7.1 from 7.2 on weaker global index breadth and wider HY and subordinated bank debt spreads, offset by strong equity inflows. Signal is Neutral.

Asset allocators remain structurally in ABB (Anything but Bonds), ABC (Anywhere but China), ABD (Anything but Dollar) and AI. They are underweight bonds and China stocks and overweight gold and US tech. 2020s annualized returns: 10-year UST -4%, China stocks (HSCEI) -5%, gold 15%, Nasdaq 17%.

Political populism keeps allocators in ABB and in structural yield curve steepeners. But higher yields now hurt the AI stock bull as bond markets police hyperscaler capex ($240bn in '24 to $1.2tn in '27E) and free cash flow ($240bn in '24 to -$180bn in '27E).
BofA expects YCC/QE threat to cap bond yields. Risk assets and AI need lower yields. The release valve in H1'27 is likely geopolitical peace, a big drop in oil and the end of rate hikes.

Proprietary indicators: Global FMS Cash Indicator 3.9% (Sell), EM Flow Trading Rule 2.8% (Sell), Global Breadth Rule -31.8% (Neutral), Global Flow Trading Rule 0.5% (Neutral), Global EPS Growth Model 35% (EPS growth rising).
